items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the general business law, in relation to the prohibition of the sale of crib bumper pads and the restriction of the use of such pads in certain settings
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S4055

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the general business law, in
relation to the prohibition of the sale of crib bumper pads and the
restriction of the use of such pads in certain settings

 PURPOSE :

To ban the sale of crib bumpers pads and restrict their use in certain
settings. This bill will prevent the deaths of and serious injury to
infants which have been attributed to the use of crib bumper pads.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1, subdivision 1, subparagraphs (a) through (i) provides a
definitions section, including a definition of crib bumper pads.

Section 1, subdivision 2 establishes the ban on sales, leases, or
offers for sale or lease of all crib bumper pads.

Section 1, subdivision 3, paragraph (a) provides that on or after the
effective date of this section, no child care facility or place of
public accommodation may use or have on its premises any crib bumper
pads. Paragraph (b) of this subdivision states that the office of
children and family services will notify child care facilities of the
provisions in this subdivision, which will enable the facilities to
effectively identify and remove crib bumper  pads. Paragraph (c)
provides that the office of children and family services shall
establish rules to comply with the ban on crib bumper pads in child
care facilities.

Section 1, subdivision 4 establishes the provisions for a violation of
subdivision 2 of this section. A court may impose a civil penalty of
not more than $500 for each violation. Each sale of a crib bumper pad
in violation of this section would constitute a separate violation.

Section 1, subdivision 5 states that provisions of this section are
severable and that if any provision of this section is held to be
unconstitutional, such invalidity will not affect other provisions
that can be given effect without the invalid provision. Section 2
provides the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

The American Academy of Pediatrics and the American Sudden Infant
Death Syndrome Institute have both issued warnings regarding the
dangers of crib bumper pads and have urged parents not to use them.
Bumper pads pose a risk of death or serious injury because babies can
get caught in the fabric and suffocate.

A study recently published in the Journal of Pediatrics reports that
nationwide, twenty-three babies died between 2006 and 2012 from
suffocation associated with the use of crib bumper pads. This number
is three times higher than the number of deaths attributable to crib
bumper pads which were recorded in the three previous six-year time
spans. Forty-eight babies died as a result of having bumper pads in
their cribs from 1985 through 2012. During this twenty-seven year time
period, an additional 146 infants were reported to have sustained
serious injuries from crib bumper pads, including choking on the
bumper pad ties or nearly suffocating.

Banning the sale of crib bumper pads would silence any confusion as to
their safety. Stores often display cribs decorated with bumper pads
which can lead to the assumption that they are in fact safe.
Prohibiting the sale of crib bumper pads and their use in certain

settings would help to avoid preventable infant deaths and ensure
children's safety in their cribs.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

None.

 FISCAL IMPACT :

No fiscal impact to the State.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the sixtieth day after it shall have
become law.

BILL NUMBER:  S4055A

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the general business law, in relation to the
prohibition of the sale of crib bumper pads and the restriction of the

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Section 1, subdivision 1, paragraphs (a) through (i) provides a
definitions section, including a definition of crib bumper pads. The
definition of crib bumper pads does not include vertical railguards

Section 1, subdivision 2 establishes the ban on sales, leases, or
offers for sale or lease of all crib bumper pads.

Section 1, subdivision 3, paragraph (a) provides that on or after the
effective date of this section, no child care facility or place of

not more than $500 for each violation.

Section 1, subdivision 5 states that provisions of this section are
severable and that if any provision of this section is held to be
unconstitutional, such invalidity will not affect other provisions
that can be given effect without the invalid provision.

Section 2 provides the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

The American Academy of Pediatrics and the American Sudden Infant
Death Syndrome Institute have both issued warnings regarding the
dangers of crib bumper pads and have urged parents not to use them.
Bumper pads pose a risk of death or serious injury because babies can

which can lead to the assumption that they are in fact safe.
Prohibiting the sale of crib bumper pads and their use in certain
settings would help to avoid preventable infant deaths and ensure

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

A.9186-B, 2016 passed Assembly.
Same as S.7041-A, 2016 referred to rules.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

No fiscal impact to the State.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the sixtieth day after it shall have
become a law.
